_doc: MIG-021v2 §1G2' bilingual lexicon for Tier 1 deterministic rules. Each entry maps a set of tokens (case-insensitive substring match against note text) to a target taxonomy ID + confidence weight. ALL targets must exist in src-tauri/src/sources/horizontal_taxonomy.rs or vertical_taxonomy.rs — invalid IDs are silently dropped at load. Drawn from Eisa's docs/sources-of-knowledge-diagram.html. Order matters: more specific / longer tokens should come first so they match before more general ones.

horizontal._comment: V3-§8.r3 (audit Epistemology #2): bare متواتر in fiqh prose almost always refers to the genus, not specifically lafẓī. Routes to PARENT mass-transmission with weight that the descend_uncertain logic will treat as 'parent class is correct, leaf is uncertain.' Specific lafẓī / maʿnawī / ʿamalī sub-classification requires more context than a token match can carry.

V3-§8.r3 (audit Epistemology #1): qiyās in Sunni uṣūl is structurally analogical INFERENCE (with shared ʿillah requirement), not comparison. Buddhist logicians (Dharmakīrti) reduce upamāna to anumāna on similar grounds. Routes to inference parent (not the comparison tree) with confidence at the parent level — descent to a specific inference sub-leaf would need disambiguation context the lexicon doesn't have.

V3-§8.r3 (audit Epistemology #2 cont.): حدثنا / أخبرنا are hadith CHAIN markers for SINGLE-NARRATOR transmission (isnād āḥād) — the OPPOSITE of tawātur. Original mapping to mass-transmission/verbal was wrong by 180 degrees. Routes to testimony/reported (a single named source's report).

V3-§8.r3 (audit Epistemology #3): Bhāṭṭa Mīmāṃsā distinguishes 4 sub-types of anupalabdhi (prāgabhāva / pradhvaṃsābhāva / anyonyābhāva / atyantābhāva). The original mapping to non-apprehension/absolute (atyantābhāva = absolute non-existence — the 'unicorn' case) was wrong for the typical missing-jar example which is prāgabhāva-or-pradhvaṃsa-neutral. Routes to PARENT non-apprehension; descent requires disambiguation context.

vertical._comment: V3-§8.r3 (audit Epistemology #5b): Sunni epistemology distinguishes iʿtiqād (fixed cognitive assent), ẓann (probable opinion — what 'I think' typically conveys in everyday Arabic), and īmān (heart-act with normative weight). The original lexicon flattened أعتقد and أظن into the same belief leaf. Now: أعتقد + 'I believe' map to belief/occurrent; أظن + 'I think that' map to opinion/probable (ẓann ghālib). al-Jurjānī, al-Taʿrīfāt.

regex_horizontal._comment: ISBN — book citation, almost always testimony/scriptural

DOI — academic paper. V3-§8 fix-B 2026-05-10: tightened to require actual DOI context (literal 'doi:' prefix or doi.org URL) — was matching too many random number/slash patterns in everyday prose. Two alternations: (1) 'doi:' / 'DOI:' / 'doi ' followed by 10.NNNN/...; (2) doi.org/10.NNNN/...
